summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in November 2024, has become the standard way to connect AI agents to external tools, data, and services. By 2026 the ecosystem spans over 9,800 tracked servers, with a durable core of individual servers (Playwright, GitHub, Context7), aggregator platforms that bundle hundreds of integrations, and gateways that handle auth, security, and routing at scale. This infrastructure matters because it turns isolated LLMs into agents that can read code, automate browsers, query databases, and act across real systems.
ecosystem_note: Individual MCP servers expose a single tool or service (e.g. GitHub, Playwright), aggregators bundle many servers behind one managed interface with unified auth, and gateways/proxies sit in front of servers to handle authentication, security, and traffic routing in production.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.connects_to: Browser automation and control — navigating pages, filling forms, scraping, running end-to-end flows and security scans across Chromium-based browsers
strengths: Highest search volume (~35,000/mo) and ranked #1 in community usage
Top scorer in MCP security scans
Browser automation is now a default install, not a niche
tools.best_for: Agents that need to drive a real browser for testing, scraping, or web interaction

tools.name: GitHub MCP
tools.connects_to: Repositories, issues, pull requests, and GitHub Actions using GitHub's own identity and permission model
strengths: Vendor-backed gold standard for code and CI workflows
Uses GitHub's native OAuth and permission model
The server most teams install first
tools.best_for: Code, CI/CD, and repository automation inside AI coding agents

tools.name: Figma MCP
tools.connects_to: Design files, components, and layouts for design-to-code agents with direct access to Figma designs
tools.pricing_paid: Requires Figma plan for file access; MCP server free
strengths: ~23,000 monthly searches, fastest-growing use case outside backend work
tools.best_for: Turning design files into code with AI agents

tools.name: Composio
tools.connects_to: Hundreds of tools (GitHub, Slack, Gmail, PostgreSQL, etc.) behind managed OAuth and a unified gateway
tools.pricing_paid: Usage-based paid tiers for managed auth and higher limits
strengths: Managed OAuth lowers maintenance burden across many servers
Strong community health and active development
tools.best_for: Teams wanting one managed gateway to connect agents to many SaaS tools

tools.name: Context7
tools.connects_to: Up-to-date library documentation and code context piped directly into the model
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans for higher usage
strengths: ~13,000 monthly searches and very widely adopted
Keeps model context current with real library docs
tools.best_for: Reducing hallucinations by giving coding agents accurate, current docs

tools.name: Supabase MCP
tools.connects_to: Supabase Postgres databases, auth, storage, and edge functions for agent-driven backend operations
tools.best_for: Agents that read/write application databases and backend services

tools.name: Notion MCP
tools.connects_to: Notion pages, databases, and workspaces for reading and writing knowledge-base content
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; Notion paid plans from $10/user/mo
tools.best_for: Agents that manage docs, notes, and structured knowledge in Notion

tools.name: n8n MCP
tools.connects_to: n8n workflow automation — triggering and orchestrating multi-step automations across 400+ integrations
strengths: Bridges agents with a mature workflow automation platform
tools.best_for: Connecting agents to complex automation workflows and third-party apps

tools.name: Zapier MCP
tools.connects_to: 7,000+ apps through Zapier's integration catalog exposed as agent-callable actions
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; Zapier paid plans from ~$20/mo
strengths: Largest breadth of SaaS integrations via one endpoint
tools.best_for: Giving agents instant reach into thousands of SaaS apps without custom servers

tools.name: Jira MCP (Atlassian)
tools.connects_to: Jira issues, projects, boards, and Confluence for project-management and issue-tracking automation
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; Atlassian paid plans vary by product
strengths: Offers a remote server with managed OAuth
tools.best_for: Agents that triage, create, and update issues in Jira/Confluence workflows

tools.name: Sequential Thinking MCP
tools.connects_to: Structured step-by-step reasoning capability that lets agents break problems into revisable thought chains
strengths: Lightweight reference server, easy to add
tools.best_for: Boosting agent reasoning on complex multi-step tasks

tools.name: Slack MCP
tools.connects_to: Slack channels, messages, and team workspaces for reading and posting messages
tools.pricing_paid: Free; Slack paid plans apply to workspace
strengths: Most widely adopted community fork (~1,800 GitHub stars), actively maintained in 2026
Managed OAuth available via gateways like Composio
tools.best_for: Agents that read and post in team Slack channels
